Official agency model runs converge on 25–28°C ranges with modest spread tied to boundary-layer mixing and urban heat-island effects, while lower-probability tails below 26°C or above 29°C align with historical rarity of extremes this early in August. Updated midday observations and afternoon model guidance will refine the exact peak before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **A broad heatwave across western Europe, driven by a strong subtropical ridge and southerly advection of warm air masses, positions mid-30s Celsius as the most likely peak for Paris on August 3.** Official guidance from Météo-France and the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) shows high pressure persisting into early August, supporting daytime maxima near or slightly above seasonal norms (typically 25–28 °C) but elevated by the fourth heat episode of the summer. Ensemble spreads remain modest, with limited thunderstorm or cloud-cover risks that could cap temperatures, while Paris’s urban heat-island effect adds 1–2 °C locally at official observation sites. Recent model runs have stabilized around 34–36 °C outcomes, aligning with market-implied probabilities that heavily favor 35 °C (45 %) and 36 °C (26.5 %) while assigning low odds to 37 °C+ or sub-34 °C results. The next ECMWF and Météo-France updates, along with any overnight minimum trends that influence daytime recovery, represent the key near-term data points that could shift the distribution.
